audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for authority dispute, vineyard tenants, cornerstone, Caesar/image, resurrection dispute, David/Lord question, and warning against scribes.

verses.restored: It happened on one of the days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and announcing good news, the chief priests and scribes with the elders stood near.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders,

modern.text: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to Him.

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ⸀ἡμερῶν διδάσκοντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λαὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εὐαγγελιζομένου ἐπέστησαν οἱ ⸀ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς σὺν τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις,

verses.restored: They spoke, saying to him, Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who is the one who gave you this authority?

familiar.text: And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?

modern.text: “Tell us,” they said, “by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?”

original.text: καὶ εἶπαν ⸂λέγοντες πρὸς αὐτόν⸃· Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς, ἢ τίς ἐστιν ὁ δούς σοι τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;

verses.restored: Answering, he said to them, I also will ask you a word; tell me:

familiar.text: And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:

modern.text: “I will also ask you a question,” Jesus replied. “Tell Me:

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς ⸀κἀγὼ λόγον, καὶ εἴπατέ μοι·

verses.restored: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from humans?

familiar.text: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?

modern.text: John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?”

original.text: Τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;

verses.restored: They reasoned together, saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say, Why did you not trust him?

familiar.text: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?

modern.text: They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe him?’

original.text: οἱ δὲ συνελογίσαντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;

verses.restored: But if we say, From humans, all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded John was a prophet.

familiar.text: But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet.

modern.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, ⸂ὁ λαὸς ἅπας⸃ καταλιθάσει ἡμᾶς, πεπεισμένος γάρ ἐστιν Ἰωάννην προφήτην εἶναι·

verses.restored: They answered that they did not know from where.

familiar.text: And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was.

modern.text: So they answered that they did not know where it was from.

original.text: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν μὴ εἰδέναι πόθεν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

modern.text: And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.” The Parable of the Wicked Tenants (Matthew 21:33–46; Mark 12:1–12)

original.text: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.

verses.restored: He began to speak this parable to the people: A person planted a vineyard, leased it to farmers, and went away for considerable times.

familiar.text: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.

modern.text: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.

original.text: Ἤρξατο δὲ πρὸς τὸν λαὸν λέγειν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· ⸀Ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν χρόνους ἱκανούς.

verses.restored: At the season he sent a servant to the farmers, so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty.

familiar.text: And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.

modern.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.

original.text: ⸀καὶ καιρῷ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς δοῦλον, ἵνα ἀπὸ τοῦ καρποῦ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ⸀δώσουσιν αὐτῷ· οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ⸂ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν δείραντες⸃ κενόν.

verses.restored: He sent another servant; but they also beat and dishonored that one and sent him away empty.

familiar.text: And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.

modern.text: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.

original.text: καὶ προσέθετο ⸂ἕτερον πέμψαι⸃ δοῦλον· οἱ δὲ κἀκεῖνον δείραντες καὶ ἀτιμάσαντες ἐξαπέστειλαν κενόν.

verses.restored: He sent a third; but they also wounded this one and threw him out.

familiar.text: And again he sent a third: and they wounded him also, and cast him out.

modern.text: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.

original.text: καὶ προσέθετο ⸂τρίτον πέμψαι⸃· οἱ δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τραυματίσαντες ἐξέβαλον.

verses.restored: The lord of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect this one.

familiar.text: Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence him when they see him.

modern.text: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.’

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος· Τί ποιήσω; πέμψω τὸν υἱόν μου τὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἴσως ⸀τοῦτον ἐντραπήσονται.

verses.restored: Seeing him, the farmers reasoned with one another, saying, This is the heir; let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.

familiar.text: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.

modern.text: But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

original.text: ἰδόντες δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γεωργοὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ⸀ἀλλήλους λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· ⸀ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, ἵνα ἡμῶν γένηται ἡ κληρονομία·

verses.restored: Throwing him outside the vineyard, they killed him. What then will the lord of the vineyard do to them?

familiar.text: So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do unto them?

modern.text: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?

original.text: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ἀπέκτειναν. τί οὖν ποιήσει αὐτοῖς ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος;

verses.restored: He will come and destroy these farmers and give the vineyard to others. Hearing this, they said, May it not happen.

familiar.text: He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.

modern.text: He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.” And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!”

original.text: ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργοὺς τούτους, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις. ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἶπαν· Μὴ γένοιτο.

verses.restored: But looking at them, he said, What then is this that has been written: The stone the builders rejected, this became the head of the corner?

familiar.text: And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?

modern.text: But Jesus looked directly at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’ ?

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς εἶπεν· Τί οὖν ἐστιν τὸ γεγραμμένον τοῦτο· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας;

verses.restored: Everyone falling on that stone will be broken; but on whomever it falls, it will crush that one.

familiar.text: Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

modern.text: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.” Paying Taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:15–22; Mark 12:13–17)

original.text: πᾶς ὁ πεσὼν ἐπʼ ἐκεῖνον τὸν λίθον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφʼ ὃν δʼ ἂν πέσῃ, λικμήσει αὐτόν.

verses.restored: The scribes and chief priests sought to lay hands on him in that hour, yet they feared the people, for they knew he spoke this parable against them.

familiar.text: And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.

modern.text: When the scribes and chief priests realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, they sought to arrest Him that very hour. But they were afraid of the people.

original.text: καὶ ἐζήτησαν οἱ ⸂γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς⸃ ἐπιβαλεῖν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν ⸂τὸν λαόν⸃, ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς ⸂εἶπεν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην⸃.

verses.restored: Watching carefully, they sent spies pretending themselves to be righteous, so that they might catch him in word, to hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.

familiar.text: And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.

modern.text: So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.

original.text: Καὶ παρατηρήσαντες ἀπέστειλαν ἐγκαθέτους ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι, ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου, ⸀ὥστε παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν τῇ ἀρχῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος.

verses.restored: They questioned him, saying, Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly and do not receive face, but teach the way of the Divine in truth.

familiar.text: And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, neither acceptest thou the person of any, but teachest the way of God truly:

modern.text: “Teacher,” they inquired, “we know that You speak and teach correctly. You show no partiality, but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.

original.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὀρθῶς λέγεις καὶ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ λαμβάνεις πρόσωπον, ἀλλʼ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις·

verses.restored: Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

familiar.text: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar, or no?

modern.text: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”

original.text: ἔξεστιν ⸀ἡμᾶς Καίσαρι φόρον δοῦναι ἢ οὔ;

verses.restored: Perceiving their craftiness, he said to them,

familiar.text: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me?

modern.text: But Jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them,

original.text: κατανοήσας δὲ αὐτῶν τὴν πανουργίαν εἶπεν πρὸς ⸀αὐτούς·

verses.restored: Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have? They said, Caesar's.

familiar.text: Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Caesar’s.

modern.text: “Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.

original.text: ⸀Δείξατέ μοι δηνάριον· τίνος ἔχει εἰκόνα καὶ ἐπιγραφήν; ⸀ἀποκριθέντες δὲ εἶπαν· Καίσαρος.

verses.restored: He said to them, Then give back the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of the Divine to the Divine.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar’s, and unto God the things which be God’s.

modern.text: So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν ⸂πρὸς αὐτούς· Τοίνυν ἀπόδοτε⸃ τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: They were not able to catch the word before the people; marveling at his answer, they were silent.

familiar.text: And they could not take hold of his words before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.

modern.text: And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people; and amazed at His answer, they fell silent. The Sadducees and the Resurrection (Matthew 22:23–33; Mark 12:18–27)

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἐπιλαβέσθαι ⸀τοῦ ῥήματος ἐναντίον τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ θαυμάσαντες ἐπὶ τῇ ἀποκρίσει αὐτοῦ ἐσίγησαν.

verses.restored: Some Sadducees, those denying there is a resurrection, came and questioned him,

familiar.text: Then came to him certain of the Sadducees, which deny that there is any resurrection; and they asked him,

modern.text: Then some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to question Him.

original.text: Προσελθόντες δέ τινες τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, οἱ ⸀ἀντιλέγοντες ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν

verses.restored: saying, Teacher, Moses wrote for us: If someone's brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up seed for his brother.

familiar.text: Saying, Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any man’s brother die, having a wife, and he die without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

modern.text: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.

original.text: λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν, ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ ἔχων γυναῖκα, καὶ οὗτος ἄτεκνος ⸀ᾖ, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: There were seven brothers. The first, taking a wife, died childless.

familiar.text: There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.

modern.text: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married a wife, but died childless.

original.text: ἑπτὰ οὖν ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος λαβὼν γυναῖκα ἀπέθανεν ἄτεκνος·

verses.restored: The second

familiar.text: And the second took her to wife, and he died childless.

modern.text: Then the second

original.text: καὶ ⸂ὁ δεύτερος⸃

verses.restored: and the third took her; likewise also the seven left no children and died.

familiar.text: And the third took her; and in like manner the seven also: and they left no children, and died.

modern.text: and the third married the widow, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.

original.text: καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἔλαβεν ⸀αὐτήν, ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐ κατέλιπον τέκνα καὶ ἀπέθανον·

verses.restored: Last, the woman also died.

familiar.text: Last of all the woman died also.

modern.text: And last of all, the woman died.

original.text: ὕστερον ⸂καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν⸃.

verses.restored: Therefore, in the resurrection, of which of them does she become wife? For the seven had her as wife.

familiar.text: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.

modern.text: So then, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”

original.text: ⸂ἡ γυνὴ οὖν ἐν τῇ⸃ ἀναστάσει τίνος αὐτῶν γίνεται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:

modern.text: Jesus answered, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.

original.text: ⸀Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου γαμοῦσιν καὶ ⸀γαμίσκονται,

verses.restored: But those considered worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.

familiar.text: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:

modern.text: But those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage.

original.text: οἱ δὲ καταξιωθέντες τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐκείνου τυχεῖν καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε ⸀γαμίζονται·

verses.restored: For neither are they able to die anymore, for they are equal to messengers and are sons of the Divine, being sons of resurrection.

familiar.text: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.

modern.text: In fact, they can no longer die, because they are like the angels. And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.

original.text: ⸀οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀποθανεῖν ἔτι δύνανται, ἰσάγγελοι γάρ εἰσιν καὶ υἱοί ⸀εἰσιν θεοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως υἱοὶ ὄντες.

verses.restored: That the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he calls the Lord the Divine of Abraham, Divine of Isaac, and Divine of Jacob.

familiar.text: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses shewed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.

modern.text: Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’

original.text: ὅτι δὲ ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροὶ καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐμήνυσεν ἐπὶ τῆς βάτου, ὡς λέγει κύριον τὸν θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ ⸀καὶ θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ ⸁καὶ θεὸν Ἰακώβ·

verses.restored: He is not Divine of dead ones but of living ones, for all live to him.

familiar.text: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.

modern.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.”

original.text: θεὸς δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων, πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν.

verses.restored: Some of the scribes answered, Teacher, you spoke beautifully/well.

familiar.text: Then certain of the scribes answering said, Master, thou hast well said.

modern.text: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, You have spoken well!”

original.text: ἀποκριθέντες δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν· Διδάσκαλε, καλῶς εἶπας·

verses.restored: For they no longer dared to question him anything.

familiar.text: And after that they durst not ask him any question at all.

modern.text: And they did not dare to question Him any further. Whose Son Is the Christ? (Matthew 22:41–46; Mark 12:35–37)

original.text: οὐκέτι ⸀γὰρ ἐτόλμων ἐπερωτᾶν αὐτὸν οὐδέν.

verses.restored: He said to them, How do they say the Messiah is David's son?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, How say they that Christ is David’s son?

modern.text: Then Jesus declared, “How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David?

original.text: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Πῶς λέγουσιν τὸν χριστὸν ⸂εἶναι Δαυὶδ υἱόν⸃;

verses.restored: For David himself says in the scroll of Psalms: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand,

familiar.text: And David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,

modern.text: For David himself says in the book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand

original.text: ⸂αὐτὸς γὰρ⸃ Δαυὶδ λέγει ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν· ⸀Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου

verses.restored: until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.

familiar.text: Till I make thine enemies thy footstool.

modern.text: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’

original.text: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.

verses.restored: David therefore calls him Lord; so how is he his son?

familiar.text: David therefore calleth him Lord, how is he then his son?

modern.text: Thus David calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?” Beware of the Scribes (Mark 12:38–40)

original.text: Δαυὶδ οὖν ⸂αὐτὸν κύριον⸃ καλεῖ, καὶ πῶς ⸂αὐτοῦ υἱός⸃ ἐστιν;

verses.restored: While all the people were hearing, he said to the disciples,

familiar.text: Then in the audience of all the people he said unto his disciples,

modern.text: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples,

original.text: Ἀκούοντος δὲ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ εἶπεν τοῖς ⸀μαθηταῖς·

verses.restored: Watch yourselves from the scribes who desire to walk around in long robes, love greetings in the marketplaces, first seats in the synagogues, and first places at dinners,

familiar.text: Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts;

modern.text: “Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.

original.text: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων περιπατεῖν ἐν στολαῖς καὶ φιλούντων ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις,

verses.restored: who devour widows' houses and for appearance make long prayers. These will receive greater judgment.

familiar.text: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a shew make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.

modern.text: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
